Recovered canonical MXNB whitepaper, reserve-management mandate; reviewed in wave 2, not a dated holdings report

reserveReview.rationale: BDO Mexico (Castillo Miranda y Compania) Q2 2026 financial valuation as of 30 June 2026 (signed 2026-07-16): a single aggregate line 'Reserves on bank accounts' MXN 35,333,251.88 against MXN 34,828,276.31 of MXNB in circulation (surplus 504,975.57). The engagement is consultancy under IVSC standards, expressly does not confirm balances with banks, and restricts use to management; its scope paragraph still says 'as of March 31, 2026' (stale copy-paste). No bank names or instrument split are disclosed. Wave-2 review of the current issuer index, October 7 aggregate dashboard and recovered canonical whitepaper found no newer weighted portfolio: the whitepaper permits pesos, cash equivalents and short-term Mexican government securities, without category weights, institution balances or maximum tenors. The historical bank-account category retains probable confidence and its original composition and review clocks; it is not restated as current holdings.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: BDO Mexico Q2 2026 valuation of MXNB reserve bank-account balances
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The Q2 valuation report does not name the reserve banks or disclose the balance at each institution, account terms, deposit protection, or direct bank confirmation. Nvio and Hey Banco are retained historical custody leads, not institutions independently identified by the Q2 report. The issuer's transparency page provides only aggregate reserves and circulation.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The whitepaper states that reserves are legally and operationally segregated from issuer and affiliate operating funds and held through a single-purpose entity. It does not establish statutory bankruptcy remoteness, current provider shares, account-level allocations, or rehypothecation treatment.
